clue.text: Time cut short with this might we presume?

definitions.text: Time cut short with this might we presume?

blocks.clueFragment: Time cut short with this might we presume?
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about how time could be abbreviated or curtailed

blocks.clueFragment: Time cut short with this might we presume?
blocks.note: setter's reading: Old Father Time is pictured carrying a mower's blade, so we presume that is what he cuts lives short with

explanation.walkthrough: 'Time' is the personified Father Time, traditionally drawn as a bearded old man carrying an hourglass and a long curved blade.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-handled curved blade is the emblem of Father Time and the Grim Reaper, who cut lives short.

clue.text: Always under cover, evacuated Darbyite in republic

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that is under another is written below it, so it comes after
a building that is evacuated is emptied, so the word loses everything between its ends

blocks.note: a cap is a covering or lid
ever means always
only the first and last letters remain once the inside is emptied

explanation.surface: A member of the Darbyite sect, always undercover, is cleared out of a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: Darbyites were the Plymouth Brethren, followers of the preacher John Nelson Darby; the surface's sense of hiding is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Verde is an island republic in the Atlantic off West Africa.

clue.text: Pint for sore head worked, saving religion for book

indicators.note: something worked has been shaped or kneaded, so these letters are rearranged
saving here means keeping safe inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A hangover cure, a pint for a sore head, worked, sparing someone's faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saving' here means keeping inside, so the religion sits within the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prisoner of Zenda is Anthony Hope's 1894 adventure novel set in a fictional kingdom.

clue.text: Odd characters from East Sheen in Ruhr location

indicators.note: odd characters are those in the first, third, fifth and further odd-numbered positions

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters

explanation.surface: Peculiar people from a London suburb turn up in Germany's industrial heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: East Sheen is a district of south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is a major industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley.

clue.text: American rule deployed in south-eastern and very old city

indicators.note: troops deployed in a place are stationed inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for south-eastern
A is the abbreviation for American
the Raj was British rule in India
V is the abbreviation for very
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An American administration sent into a south-eastern, ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarajevo is the capital city of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

clue.text: Everything and nothing close to Verica's town

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

blocks.note: all means everything
O looks like zero, nothing
the final letter of this name

explanation.surface: Everything or nothing lies near the town belonging to Verica, an ancient British king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a town in Clackmannanshire, central Scotland.

clue.text: Struggled to be heard after orchestra's last gong

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter, the only one used
something to be heard is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: the final letter of orchestra
warred, meaning fought or struggled, said out loud

explanation.surface: A musician fights to be audible over the orchestra's final gong stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is British slang for a medal or honour, not the percussion instrument the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is informal British slang for a medal or decoration, an award.

clue.text: Skill needed to load what's a medium-sized revolver?

indicators.note: loading means filling a gun or vehicle, so this piece is packed inside the other

blocks.note: eh? is a way of saying what?
art means skill

explanation.surface: Skill is needed to load a mid-size revolver, a handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a gun, but it is a planet revolving round the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is a mid-sized planet that revolves around the Sun.

clue.text: See 3
Leading TV soap's initial troubles

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter of a word, the only one kept

blocks.note: a team that is leading is up
a TV is a television set
the first letter of soap

explanation.surface: The opening episode of a hit TV soap opera stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV soap' reads as one phrase, but TV and soap are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset is to disturb or distress, so upsets is a verb form matching troubles.

clue.text: Jailhouse Rock from Mozart – a classic recalled?

indicators.note: taken from these words means the letters are lifted straight out of the printed run
to recall is to call back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the run of letters tucked inside these words, read in the printed direction

explanation.surface: Was Elvis's hit Jailhouse Rock borrowed from a Mozart classic?
explanation.walkthrough: Jailhouse Rock is an Elvis Presley song, but here it means a prison on a rock, nicknamed The Rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was a notorious federal prison on a rocky island in San Francisco Bay, known as The Rock.

clue.text: Renowned, the Navy at sea from time to time

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The famous Navy goes out to sea now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for occasionally, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Indolent Huxley discontented with his entire output?

indicators.note: read as dis-contented, with its contents removed, leaving only the ends of the name

blocks.note: a writer's collected works are their entire output
with its contents emptied, only the first and last letters stay

explanation.surface: Was the writer Aldous Huxley idle, dissatisfied with everything he produced?
explanation.definitionFit: Workshy describes someone who avoids work, so lazy or indolent.

clue.text: Partridge perhaps ascending to embrace unknown creature

indicators.note: in a down answer, ascending means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top
embracing someone means wrapping arms around them, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: Alan Partridge is Steve Coogan's comic TV character
Y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A game bird flies up and wraps itself round a strange beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partridge' looks like the bird, but it is Alan Partridge, a British sitcom character; 'perhaps' signals the example.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa, so a creature.

clue.text: What might be despot's ending – incendiary going off?

definitions.text: What might be despot's ending – incendiary going off?

indicators.note: a word's ending is its final letter, which is all that is used
a bomb going off explodes, scattering the letters into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of despot
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firebomb exploding could be how a tyrant meets his end.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: an assassination by bomb is one way a despot might end.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrannicide is the killing of a tyrant, the end of a despot.

clue.text: Combatant with others joining the French Resistance

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the rest means the others
le is French for the
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fighter teams up with comrades to join the wartime French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French Resistance' reads as the wartime movement, but the French gives LE and Resistance just R.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrestler is a fighter in a grappling bout, so a type of combatant.

clue.text: Cheerful after tenancy comes to stop

indicators.note: one piece placed after another is written following it in the answer

blocks.note: a let is a tenancy or lease
to be up is to be in good spirits

explanation.surface: Someone is happy when their lease finally comes to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or cessation, as in no let-up in the rain.

clue.text: Dawn where subtle emanation covers over river

indicators.note: something that covers another wraps round it, so the second piece sits inside

blocks.note: an aura is a subtle glow or emanation said to surround a person
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A description of daybreak as a faint glow spreading over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Latin name for dawn, and the Roman goddess of daybreak.

clue.text: Hope setting sun bathes woman in college

indicators.note: the sun bathes something by surrounding it with light, so it goes round the rest
a woman in a place is inside it, so her name sits within the other word

blocks.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
uni is short for university
Rita is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A sun-loving optimist describes a woman sunbathing at university.
explanation.walkthrough: Hope is Anthony Hope, author of the novel at 3/9, not the feeling; the sun god wraps round everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional kingdom where Anthony Hope set his novels, so Hope's setting.

clue.text: Proteinous seed a gym enthusiast ingests

indicators.note: to ingest is to swallow, so the small piece goes inside the larger one

blocks.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
taken as written
a nut is a fanatic or enthusiast

explanation.surface: A fitness fanatic eats a protein-rich seed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gym enthusiast' reads as one person, a fitness fan, but it splits into two pieces either side of the A.
explanation.definitionFit: The peanut is a legume seed prized as a rich source of protein.

clue.text: Go on piano by conductor

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor urges a pianist to continue playing.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on is idiomatic for talking at length, and to prattle is to chatter on.

clue.text: Flanders collaborator really losing face: it's for the birds

indicators.note: a word's face is its front, so losing it drops the opening letter

blocks.note: Donald Swann wrote comic songs with Michael Flanders as Flanders and Swann
very means really

explanation.surface: A wartime Flanders collaborator really loses face, a thing worth nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Flanders and Swann were a British comedy-song duo of the 1950s and 60s; the face of really is its first letter, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A swannery is a place where swans are bred and kept, literally a facility for birds.

clue.text: Sacristy with His pots vandalised? We look to the Heavens!

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church vestry and the Lord's vessels have been wrecked, and the faithful look heavenward in despair.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrophysicists study stars and galaxies, so they literally look up to the heavens for their work.

clue.text: Supporter on Thursday shows effectiveness

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
Th is the abbreviation for Thursday

explanation.surface: A fan turning out on Thursday proves their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, one piece on another sits above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeth means power to enforce, as in a law with teeth, so effectiveness.

clue.text: Group under religious rule right to dam German river

indicators.note: a dam sits across a river, blocking it from within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the Oder runs along the German-Polish border
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sect under strict rules has the right to dam a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious order is a community of monks or nuns living under a common rule.

clue.text: Plant found in Madras as locals know it?

indicators.note: what is found in a word lies inside it, so its outer letters fall away

blocks.note: Madras is now officially Chennai, its Tamil name

explanation.surface: A plant is found in the Indian city, called by its local name.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters are not in the clue's words but in the name they point to, Chennai.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a flowering shrub whose leaves give a reddish dye.

clue.text: Star player Jeremy works with the press?

blocks.note: first meaning: Jeremy ..., the Oscar-winning actor
second meaning: presses clothes flat with a hot appliance

explanation.walkthrough: 'Works with the press' suggests journalism, but it means pressing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Irons is a star actor, and someone who irons smooths clothes by pressing them.

clue.text: Demise in Hertfordshire town much-followed on X

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so this piece goes within the town

blocks.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England
a demise is an end

explanation.surface: A death in a small English town becomes a hot topic on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: X is the social network formerly called Twitter.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic trending on social media is one currently attracting lots of posts and attention.

clue.text: Direct from Rabelais, nothing found in books

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
rien is French for nothing, and Rabelais was a French writer

explanation.surface: Instructions taken straight out of a French satirist's works.
explanation.definitionFit: To orient someone is to point them in the right direction, much as to direct them.

clue.text: Impalpable in the present life cryptic tale captures

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and obscure, so the letters are disguised in a new order
to capture is to hold inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
here, as opposed to the hereafter, means in this present life

explanation.surface: A mysterious story conveys something intangible about our life now.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, too light to be touched, so impalpable.

clue.text: Recognise cutting tool's back-and-forth motion

blocks.note: to see is to recognise
a saw is a toothed cutting tool

explanation.surface: Spotting how a saw moves to and fro as it cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesaw is used for any alternating up-and-down or to-and-fro movement, as well as the playground plank.
